opening_message:
Ticket 1: Nancy Hunter (employee ID E038) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E038.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Nancy Hunter (E038) is a full-time Engineer requesting admin access to Payroll. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so admin is not permitted for Engineers. Max level is write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Nancy Hunter (E038) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors are limited to read unless they have advanced training, and never admin. Admin request exceeds the maximum, so recommend granting read.
reason: Nancy Hunter (E038) requested admin access to Payroll. Admin is never permitted for contractors, and for full-time employees admin is only allowed if their role owns the system; Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, and Nancy is an Engineer, so admin is not permitted either way. However, the HR and Security notes conflict on employment type (HR: full_time; Security: contractor, looked up in the Security DB, with basic security training). Based on the Security agent's verified record (contractor with basic training), contractor maximum is read. Since the requested admin level exceeds the maximum, grant the maximum of read. This is also the most conservative level given the conflicting employment-type records.

Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee: Nancy Hunter (E038)
Request: admin access to Payroll

Two notes with conflicting information:
- HR agent: full_time Engineer, recommends write for Payroll
- Security agent: contractor with basic security training, recommends read

The HR agent looked up role in own database. Security agent looked up employment type and security training in own database but did NOT look up role (used HR's value).

Conflict: employment type differs. HR says full_time, Security says contractor.

The access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist role. Nancy is an Engineer, so even if full-time, admin is not allowed for Payroll (role doesn't own system). If full-time: max write. If contractor with basic training: max read.

Requested: admin. Max is write (if full-time) or read (if contractor). Either way, admin is above max. So grant the maximum.

Which maximum? Need to decide based on the facts. The HR agent says full_time; security agent says contractor. Conflict in employment type.

Actually the security agent's note says employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing). HR note says full_time (looked up in own database before writing). Both claim to have looked it up. Conflict.

Also security training: basic (looked up). So contractor with basic training → read.

Given conflicting information, which to trust? The security agent's note includes both employment type and security training, both looked up. HR note includes employment type and role.

Hmm, this is ambiguous. Let me look carefully at the notes:

HR note: "role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing); employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing); recommendation for Payroll: write"

Security note: "role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent); employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing); security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing); recommendation for Payroll: read"

I'll submit read.
